title: EXP-058 — Hello World Part 3 Section 8: FX_Items Custom FX_Test Event Migration and Runtime Verification
objective: On the existing User-scoped FX_Items Form, move exactly the two original handler actions from StdFormRefreshCompleted to a custom event named FX_Test by changing each action's Event To Handle > Event value. Preserve sequence 0 Prompt with its Hello World and OK configuration, and sequence 1 Set Values with SETVARVALUES(FX_VarTest=P(FX_Description)). Change only FX_RefreshButton's Primary event from StdFormRefresh to FX_Test. Verify that FX_Test contains exactly those two original actions and that no StdFormRefreshCompleted handler remains on FX_Items. Perform one ordinary Designer Save, close and reopen the scoped Form, and verify definition recovery. Then close the inherited clean runtime FX_Items tab and open the Form exactly once. Verify that initial opening loads all three records without a Hello World prompt and that FX_VarTestEdit is initially empty. Activate FX_Refresh exactly once, capture and dismiss the expected Hello World prompt, and compare the resulting variable-bound Edit value with the current record's FX_Description. Record all observations, limitations, and action counts without further mutation.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md, the relevant agent boundary, and hello-world-pt3.md Section 8 (07:39–08:31) as task instructions and reference material. Review EXP-055, EXP-056, and EXP-057 evidence before operating the browser.
Capture the inherited Designer and Web Client states before any mutation. Identify both browser tabs without modifying their contents.
Verify the exact FX_Items Form identity using Name FX_Items, ScopeType User, and ScopeName matching EXP-057. Confirm a usable Designer session, disabled Save, and no outstanding dialogs.

Capture a complete pre-mutation baseline: Initial Command Refresh, all 17 components, Name, Type, Data Source, Pane, Container, Tab, bindings, Location, Size, and exposed event properties. Explicitly inspect FX_RefreshButton, FX_DescriptionEdit, and FX_VarTestEdit.
Verify exactly one StdFormRefreshCompleted handler group with sequence 0 Prompt and sequence 1 Set Values. Inspect their native parameter readbacks and enabled states before modification.
Independently verify the FX_VarTest definition in the Form - Temporary Variables category, recording Persistent False, Global False, and its displayed Value without changing it.
Verify the FX_Test destination does not already contain conflicting handler actions before migration.

Move sequence 0 Prompt by changing only its Event To Handle > Event value from StdFormRefreshCompleted to FX_Test. Use the existing Event combobox or its documented editable entry when FX_Test is not listed. Capture the intermediate state and record whether FX_Test appeared automatically.
Move sequence 1 Set Values to the same FX_Test event using the same native property route. Reinspect both action identities and exact parameter values after migration.
Verify before Save that exactly one FX_Test group contains the two original actions in their original order, neither is duplicated, and the StdFormRefreshCompleted group no longer contains a handler.
Change only FX_RefreshButton > Events > Primary from StdFormRefresh to FX_Test. Preserve its Name, Caption, component Type, Binding Type, Binding, Location, Size, Tab, and remaining Events.

Capture the complete before-Save comparison against the initial baseline, verifying that Initial Command, all 17 components, FX_VarTestEdit binding, FX_VarTest definition, and all unrelated Form properties remain unchanged.
Perform exactly one ordinary native Designer Save after the complete migration has been validated. Capture the Save outcome and verify the Designer becomes clean with Save disabled.

Close the clean Designer FX_Items Form tab exactly once. Reopen through the Form menu's recent-forms FX_Items entry, permitting one retry after a fresh menu snapshot if the first attempt times out. If both attempts fail, permit one native Designer Open toolbar and Select Form alternative for the exact FX_Items identity.

After Designer reopening, verify Name, ScopeType, ScopeName, the FX_Test handler and both actions, absence of the old handler, FX_RefreshButton Primary FX_Test, unchanged components, unchanged FX_VarTest definition, Initial Command Refresh, and Save disabled.
Close the inherited clean Web Client FX_Items runtime Form tab once, then open FX_Items once using native Web Client Open > Select Form.

Observe the fully opened runtime Form before any button activation. Capture all three original records, current row, Description, runtime Save-disabled state, absence of a Hello World prompt, and the initial FX_VarTestEdit display value.
Activate the rendered FX_Refresh button exactly once. Capture the expected Hello World prompt before one authorized OK dismissal.
After the prompt dismissal, capture the selected record identity, FX_Description value, inferred FX_VarTestEdit display value, and exact equality comparison.

Record screenshots, accessibility snapshots, action counts, unexpected states, evidence limitations, final acceptance matrix, and repository confinement under evidence/EXP-058/. Write or update only the EXP-058 experiment record and its evidence directory.

acceptance_checks.description: Read-only preflight confirms the inherited Designer and runtime tabs, a usable Designer session, exact FX_Items Form identity (Name + User scope + matching ScopeName), clean Save-disabled state, and no session challenge or error dialog. Separate screenshots and accessibility snapshots are saved under evidence/EXP-058/. The tutorial Section 8 and its agent boundary have been reviewed.

A complete pre-mutation baseline establishes one StdFormRefreshCompleted group with exactly two enabled actions: sequence 0 Prompt with Hello World and OK configuration, and sequence 1 Set Values with SETVARVALUES(FX_VarTest=P(FX_Description)). Initial Command is Refresh. All 17 original component entries and their exposed properties, bindings, geometry, and events are captured. FX_RefreshButton Primary is StdFormRefresh, FX_VarTestEdit binds variables.FX_VarTest, FX_VarTest is Form - Temporary, and no conflicting FX_Test handler exists. Capture decisive grid screenshots, native property readbacks, and unavailable fields.

Before Save, exactly the original sequence 0 Prompt and sequence 1 Set Values actions are associated with one FX_Test event group, with their original parameter values, order, and enabled states intact. There are exactly two handler actions total and no remaining StdFormRefreshCompleted handler on FX_Items. Captured intermediate and final grids demonstrate actual movement rather than copying. Evidence records whether FX_Test was offered by the picker or accepted through native combobox entry.

Before Save, FX_RefreshButton Events > Primary equals FX_Test. All other button properties match the AC-2 baseline. The complete 17-component inventory, FX_VarTestEdit binding and geometry, FX_DescriptionEdit property binding, FX_VarTest definition, Initial Command Refresh, and unrelated Form properties remain unchanged. Screenshots and property snapshots establish the comparison, with discrepancies explicitly recorded.

Exactly one native Designer Save completes successfully after the entire migration. The Designer becomes clean with Save disabled and no error dialog. A post-Save readback still shows the single FX_Test group with both original actions, no StdFormRefreshCompleted handler, FX_RefreshButton Primary FX_Test, and unchanged comparison properties. Capture the Save result and post-Save clean-state screenshot.

The clean FX_Items Designer Form tab is closed once and the exact User-scoped Form is reopened through the bounded native sequence: recent-forms entry once, one fresh-menu retry if needed, and at most one Designer Open > Select Form fallback if both fail. The recovered Form retains exactly the FX_Test actions, their sequence and parameters, FX_RefreshButton Primary FX_Test, all 17 components, FX_VarTest definition, Initial Command Refresh, and Save disabled. The evidence records every attempted route and exact counts. This proves observed UI recovery across ordinary close/reopen, not independent database durability.

The inherited clean FX_Items Web Client runtime tab is closed exactly once and FX_Items is opened exactly once through native Open > Select Form. The settled Form loads the original three item records with unchanged values and Initial Command Refresh behavior, without any Hello World prompt. Capture the reopening route, fully rendered Form, selected record, Save-disabled state, and fresh settled accessibility snapshots before any FX_Refresh activation. An opening-time prompt fails this check and stops runtime execution.

After runtime opening and before FX_Refresh, the value box corresponding by position and Designer binding to FX_VarTestEdit is visibly empty, with no error. Capture both screenshot and accessibility value readback. Explicitly qualify any lack of a runtime accessibility name. A nonempty value or missing component fails this expected initial-state postcondition; no repair or extra opening is permitted.

Exactly one native FX_Refresh activation produces exactly one Hello World prompt on FX_Items. A screenshot and accessibility snapshot capture the prompt's text, Form title, and OK response before one authorized dismissal. A missing prompt, multiple prompts, or unexpected dialog is a failed postcondition and does not authorize another click.

After the single authorized prompt dismissal, the FX_VarTestEdit-associated display value equals the selected row's actual FX_Description character-for-character. For dumbbell the expected value is 45 pound iron; for eggs cage free; for guitar natural acoustic. Capture the selected item, actual Description, value-box readback, and visual comparison in the same evidence sequence. The original records remain unchanged and runtime Save disabled. The test establishes the observed custom-event runtime result only.

The final report reconciles exactly two action migrations, one FX_RefreshButton Primary change, one Designer Save, one Designer close and authorized reopen route, one inherited runtime Form closure, one runtime opening, zero opening-time Hello World prompts, one FX_Refresh activation, one refresh-triggered Hello World prompt, and at most one corresponding OK dismissal. Zero unauthorized metadata changes, zero business-data modifications, and zero extra activations are supported by the recorded action audit. A complete AC-1 through AC-11 matrix cites decisive evidence. Repository confinement verifies that worker-authored changes are restricted to the EXP-058 experiment record and evidence/EXP-058/, with pre-existing changes and automatic ignored captures separately disclosed. Outcome classification is observed or blocked as supported, never replay_verified.

notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261011-172309-X5Gt. Rationale: EXP-057 established the existing User-scoped FX_Items definition, two ordered StdFormRefreshCompleted actions, FX_VarTest Form-Temporary variable, FX_VarTestEdit binding, and functioning Hello World prompts on initial opening and refresh. Section 8 requires changing the event that owns those existing actions, rather than creating additional handlers. This experiment tests that single functional migration through one Designer Save, ordinary close/reopen recovery, and a discriminating runtime comparison between initial Form opening and explicit FX_Refresh activation. It also incorporates EXP-055's lesson that full component properties, bindings, geometry, and events must be captured before mutation. EXP-057 was the continuation of tutorial Section 7; EXP-058 addresses the actual Section 8. | Operator review 2026-10-11: removed SaveChanges from the lifecycle pattern (the single Designer Save is planned) and added Form Sync/Deploy; dropped "remove" from the delete pattern (moving the actions removes them from StdFormRefreshCompleted by design) and "edit" from the typing pattern (it matched the component name FX_VarTestEdit); exact_values FX_Items, FX_Test (case-sensitive typing guard); deny_browser_javascript; User editing scope. Operator decision: no diagnostics. Approval pending from the operator.
